incident: BazarCall to Conti ransomware via Trickbot and Cobalt Strike

sources.title: BazarCall to Conti Ransomware via Trickbot and Cobalt Strike - The DFIR Report (2021-08-01)
sources.what_it_gave: entry (BazarCall -> malicious Excel -> Trickbot -> Cobalt Strike), hops (WMIC 165.bat to two hosts, CS loader via service on another, Conti staged on DC share and PsExec to all domain-joined), exfil (AD forest data), impact (Conti [KCRAO] domain-wide), ~2 days

narrative_before: In this 2021 intrusion the DFIR Report observed a BazarCall campaign: a malicious macro-enabled Excel file (cancel_sub_VCP1234567890123.xlsx) installed Trickbot, which downloaded a Cobalt Strike beacon on the beachhead host. The actors used WMIC to run 165.bat on two other hosts, then a PowerShell Cobalt Strike loader via a service with SYSTEM. The Conti payload was staged in a share (C:\share$) on a domain controller, and two batch scripts (_COPY.bat, _EXE.bat) used PsExec with a domain account to copy and run Conti on all domain-joined computers (target lists comps1.txt/comps5.txt), encrypting files with the [KCRAO] extension. AD-forest data (usernames, DC configuration, machine enumeration) was exfiltrated during discovery. The MITRE mapping lists LSASS and NTDS dumping. The operators returned about two days later for the ransomware phase.

detection_moments.description: BazarCall-delivered Trickbot running on the beachhead and loading a Cobalt Strike beacon.
detection_moments.evidence: 'The threat actors used BazarCall to install Trickbot in the environment ... Trickbot downloaded and ran a Cobalt Strike Beacon' - BazarCall to Conti, The DFIR Report

detection_moments.description: WMIC runs 165.bat on two hosts, then a Cobalt Strike PowerShell loader runs via a service as SYSTEM; AD-forest data exfiltrated during discovery.
detection_moments.evidence: 'Two unnamed hosts: Received 165.bat via WMIC, then a Cobalt Strike PowerShell loader ... Entire AD forest data ... was exfiltrated' - BazarCall to Conti

detection_moments.description: Return ~2 days later: Conti staged in C:\share$ on a DC; _COPY.bat/_EXE.bat use PsExec to copy and run Conti on all domain-joined computers ([KCRAO]).
detection_moments.evidence: 'The Conti payload was staged in a share on a DC, at C:\share$ ... Conti was copied to and run on all domain-joined computers, using target lists' - BazarCall to Conti

attack_path: BazarCall malicious Excel installs Trickbot which downloads Cobalt Strike (T1566.001/T1204.002)
WMIC remotely executes 165.bat then Cobalt Strike PowerShell loader (T1047)
Conti payload staged in C:\share$ on the domain controller (T1021.002)
PsExec (_COPY.bat/_EXE.bat) copies and runs Conti on all domain-joined computers (T1021.002/T1486)
ambiguities: Hosts named by role only except the DC; victim sector not stated. Generic domain-joined computers modelled as srv_1/pc_4.
No absolute timestamps; time to ransom ~2 days (approximate).
LSASS/NTDS dumping appears only in the MITRE mapping, not the narrative; domain admin not explicitly confirmed.
Exfil tool not named. Moments are the report's activity markers, not a defender detection timeline.
